title: How many switches does two-Hamiltonian universality require?
abstract: Any pair of sufficiently generic Hamiltonians on $\mathbb{C}^d$ generates the full unitary group, i.e., any $W\in U(d)$ can be synthesized to arbitrary precision by alternating between the two evolutions for suitably chosen durations. For any given pair of Hamiltonians, the minimal number of switches required to cover the entire group is at least $d$ and unbounded in general. Despite this, we show that it scales linearly in $d$ in expectation. Assuming that the two spectra are sufficiently generic, we derive constructive upper bounds on the minimal switching number as a function of the change-of-basis matrix between the two eigenbases. In particular, if this matrix has a column whose entries all have equal moduli, as for a complex Hadamard matrix, then $9d$ switches suffice to reach every unitary. To obtain these results, we construct a short exact representation of any unitary as a product of unitaries that are alternately diagonal in two given bases. All bounds are extended to non-generic spectra and bounded evolution times.
summary: This paper analyzes the problem of 'two-Hamiltonian universality,' determining the minimum number of times one must switch between two fixed Hamiltonian controls to generate any desired unitary transformation in a quantum system. It establishes that this required number scales linearly with the system dimension $d$ for generic cases. The results provide crucial theoretical bounds for quantum control protocols, which are vital for quantum computing and simulation.
main_problem: The paper determines the minimal number of alternating Hamiltonian switches required to synthesize any arbitrary unitary evolution in a $d$-dimensional quantum system.
main_result: For generic Hamiltonians, the required number of switches scales linearly with the dimension $d$ in expectation, and specific bounds (like $9d$) are derived for certain structured cases.
method: The authors relate the problem to finding the minimal length representation of unitaries as products of elements diagonal in two different eigenbases, utilizing techniques from group theory and graph theory.
model_or_system: The model involves a $d$-dimensional quantum system whose evolution is governed by alternating unitary operators derived from two fixed Hamiltonians, $H_1$ and $H_2$.
key_observables: The minimal number of switches ($n$ or $\ell$) required to achieve a target unitary $W \in U(d)$, and the approximation error $\|W - V\|$.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$, the structure of the change-of-basis matrix between the two eigenbases, and the spectral properties (linear independence over $\mathbb{Q}$) of the eigenvalues.
main_assumptions: The main results often assume the spectra of the Hamiltonians are sufficiently generic (eigenvalues linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$), although bounds are extended to non-generic cases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general problem of two-Hamiltonian universality to deriving constructive upper bounds using representations of unitaries via Householder reflections, culminating in explicit bounds on the required number of switches and approximation errors.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, quantitative bounds on the complexity of quantum control, which is fundamental to designing quantum gates and understanding the limitations of physical implementations of quantum algorithms.
